text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Under the Howard Government's A$620 million small business reform package, companies with 15 workers or less will be exempt from Federal unfair dismissal rules in employees' first year, meaning they will find it easier to fire new staff. Business response to the radical package has been mixed, with many industry groups saying it does not go far enough. Page 1.

ACTU secretary Bill Kelty has outlined a plan which would see middle-aged workers facing redundancy offered a gradual retirement from the workforce. Saying that those over the age of 45 face significant barriers to re-renter the workforce, workers would be offered an additional six months employment on a part-time basis. Page 3.

Members of the West Australian police force's Official Corruption Investigation Unit are believed to have accumulated enough evidence to charge former Federal Health Minister Carmen Lawrence for perjury after Commissioner Kenneth Marks found in 1995 she led during questioning at the Easton Royal Commission. However, the Unit is so far undecided on whether to charge the Labor frontbencher. Page 3.

A report from the Electronic Commerce Taskforce of the Commonwealth Law Enforcement Board has found that Australia is one of the world leaders in anti-laundering measures but would be the big loser if on-line tax evasion and criminal activity hit the Intenet. It also found that despite its status, little is being done to avert the potential problem. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following months of political campaigning and debate about the Northern Territory's controversial 1995 right-to-die laws, which have already been used by four people to be assisted in their deaths, the Euthanasia Laws Bill, introduced by Victorian Liberal MP Kevin Andrews to overturn the euthanasia laws, passed a preliminary vote in the Senate last night. Page 1.

Under the Federal Government's long-awaited, A$750 million assistance package for small businesses, unveiled by Prime Minister John Howard yesterday, only a minority of Australia's 900,000 small firms look set to benefit directly from limited tax breaks ad up to 600,000 small businesses will be given virtually unlimited rights to fire new staff. Page 1.

Following her appointment as head of the Office of the Status of Women, Radio National's Pru Goward, who has worked at the ABC for almost 20 years, has been banned by the national broadcaster from asking probing questions and speaking with other media outets until she assumes her new position on April 21. Page 1.

Senior Government ministers supported controversial Independent Senator Mal Colston yesterday after it was revealed Colston, the deputy president of the Senate, paid back almost A$7,000 to cover anomalies in his expense claims, which he says were caused by "inadequate book-keeping" in his office. However, Federal Police may be asked to examine Colston's claims for allowances, with further discrepancies allegedly under investigation. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As supporters of Liberal MP Kevin Andrews' private member's Bill against the Northern Territory's euthanasia legislation claimed a lead of five firm votes, 35 - 30, in the Senate last night, outspoken euthanasia advocate Philip Nitschke said he would not bandon the two patients who have already completed the necessary paperwork to use the right-to-die law. Page 1.

Responding to the report of a Senate inquiry which found he had been overpaid travel allowances on 31 occasions, Senator Mal Colston has blamed "sloppy book-keeping" by Christine Smith, a senior staffer, for his claiming of A$6,880 in travelling allowance for 43 days that he did not travel - a claim accepted by the Federal Government. Page 1.

As part of a strategy to lower costs and reduce its present 300 branches to 60 key branches, Colonial State Bank launched a wide-ranging scheme yesterday which will see it offering most of its branches throughout Australia for franchising. The move gives people the chance to run a bank branch at a possible A$200,000 a year profit. Page 1.

Connections of the Australian movie Shine gathered in America yesterday on the eve of this year's Academy Awards to be announced tonight. Best male actor favourite Geoffrey Rush has admitted he is nervous before the big decision and says he hopes not to get a touch of the 'Anna Paquins', the dumb-struck 11-year-old winner of the 1994 best supporting actress, if he wins tonight. Page 3.
THE AGE

In a decision which is set to end the Northern Territory's world-first system of legalised euthanasia, the Senate voted 38 to 34 to pass a private member's Bill, initiated by Victorian MP Kevin Andrews, and override the controversial right-to-die law. Pag 1.

Health authorities in Victoria said yesterday 243 people were suffering food poisoning which was linked backed to the World Hot Bread shop in Springvale. The Human Services Department has ordered a two week closure of the bakery, which was recently warned about its hygiene standards by the local council. Page A1.

Independent Senator Mal Colston has blamed "inadequate book-keeping" by Christine Smith - his staff member who received a A$10,000 pay rise after a prime ministerial intervention last year - for his payment travel allowances on 43 nights since July 1993 fr being in one city when he wasn't. Colston yesterday repaid A$6,880 to taxpayers to compensate for the falsely claimed allowance. Page 1.

In a surprise move welcomed by the women's movement and political parties, Prime Minister Howard has appointed Pru Goward, prominent ABC Radio National political reporter who also runs her own media consultancy, as the head of the Office of the Status of omen, one of the most senior jobs in the bureaucracy. Page 1.
